Thank you for your interest in Cal Poly Maritime Academy!  

California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo and Cal Poly Maritime Academy has integrated into one university with two locations. Cal Poly Maritime Academy will be known as Solano Campus. Each respective campus will maintain separate assist.org accounts until Fall 2028, when our curriculum is fully integrated. 

 

This articulation agreement displays the lower-division courses required in major and support. Students are advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer.  

GENERAL INFORMATION

  • University Catalog for the full listing of degree requirements for this major
  • Admissions website for current transfer admission requirements for Solano campus
  • Cal Poly Maritime Academy website for information for Solano campus 

ACADEMIC INFORMATION

  • Requirements and flowcharts for each major can be viewed on the respective major page, under the requirements tab. Information about concentrations, if applicable, are displayed on this page
  • AP/IB/CLEP credit
  • Academic Advising  
  • Transfer Credits at Cal Poly | Cal Poly and Cal Poly Maritime Academy are one university with two locations. There will be two separate Assist.org accounts until Fall 2028, when our curriculum is fully integrated.

The Bachelor of Arts in International Security and Strategy requires a minimum of 120 units consisting of general education, major, and graduation requirements. This agreement only lists the lower division major requirements.﻿


The International Strategy and Security (ISS) major offered by the Department of Philosophy is the only undergraduate major of its kind in the United States. Several of our courses are offered only at Cal Poly Maritime Academy and help provide the foundation for the newest degree program on campus. The ISS Program focuses on strategic, interdisciplinary studies across national, international and maritime domains—with an emphasis on the most relevant security challenges facing the nation and the global community today. Students will build skills in oral and written communication, critical thinking, problem solving, leadership development, policy analysis, research methods, and quantitative analysis.
